answer: A concrete defense is stake-backed identity: each agent must lock a deposit to receive a signed credential, like a ferrous anchor that is expensive to forge. Sybil attackers must then multiply their capital instead of spawning free identities. Peers track behavioral reputation -- a raven watcher that logs uptime and attestation honesty -- and slash deposits when misconduct is detected. All claims ride on a zero-knowledge cipher handshake, so one deposit cannot be double-spent across identities. Faking a thousand agents costs a thousand stakes, making attacks unprofitable.
